newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh halts repatriation after violence.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh halts repatriation after violence.

text.p: Bangladesh postponed repatriation of Burmese refugees on Thursday after militant protests over alleged attempts to forcibly return them.
"We have cancelled today's repatriation of some 200 Rohingya Moslems as we don't want to inflame violence in the refugee camps," repatriation official Qamrul Huda said.
"We don't want to force anyone to go back," he told Reuters in Cox's Bazar, bordering west Burma's Moslem-majority Arakan province.
Other officials said Thursday's repatriation attempts were aborted after Rohingyas refusing to go back put on red headbands, carried sticks and knives, and chanted demands to stay in Bangladesh.
"We must resist bids to push us across the (Naf) river into death traps in Burma," one official quoted a protester at Kutupalong camp as saying.
Authorities had earlier stopped repatriation from Nayapara camp after violence on Sunday left nearly 20 people injured, including six policemen.
They planned to repatriate some 200 Rohingyas from Kutupalong on Thursday. "But it seemed to be too risky given the high-running tension," one official told Reuters.
It was not known when repatriation would resume.

Bangladesh foreign office officials said on Wednesday the resistance against repatriation was rooted in a recent United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) proposal to the government to allow the remaining 21,000 refugees from the 1992 influx to live permanently in Bangladesh.
"The refugees began resisting as soon as the information of the UNHCR proposal was leaked out to the camps. That is the crux of the problem," said one senior official.
